executive_summary:
⚡ QUICK REVISION SUMMARY:
• This lecture provides an in-depth exploration of HTML5 multimedia embedding using native elements.
• It details the syntax and behavior of the <video> and <audio> tags, explains media control attributes (controls, autoplay, muted, loop, poster), demonstrates multi-format source fallbacks, and illustrates embedding third-party media streams using <iframe>.
learning_objectives: Configure controls, muted autoplay policies, loop, and poster images
Provide cross-browser format fallbacks with nested <source> tags
Safely embed external third-party media using the <iframe> element

sections.heading: 1. HTML5 <video> Element & Playback Attributes
sections.content:
• The HTML5 <video> element embeds video streams directly without browser plugins.
• Key attributes include 'controls' (renders browser player UI), 'poster' (displays preview placeholder image), and 'autoplay' (requires 'muted' to satisfy modern browser user autoplay policies).
code_snippets:
<video src="media/sample.mp4" controls width="640" poster="thumbnail.jpg">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

sections.heading: 2. HTML5 <audio> Tag & Format Fallbacks
sections.content:
• The <audio> element streams audio files.
• Because browser codec support varies, developers enclose multiple <source> elements (MP3, OGG, WAV) inside <audio> to ensure resilient playback across all operating systems.
code_snippets:
<audio controls autoplay muted>
  <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  <source src="podcast.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>

sections.heading: 3. Third-Party Embedding with <iframe>
sections.content:
• The <iframe> (Inline Frame) element embeds external web documents and media players (such as YouTube or Google Maps).
• It uses 'src', 'width', 'height', 'title', and 'allowfullscreen' attributes.

definitions_and_terms.definition: HTML5 element used to play video clips natively in browsers.
Boolean attribute that exposes browser play, pause, seek, and volume UI.
Inline frame element embedding nested browsing contexts.

common_pitfalls: Attempting unmuted autoplay, which modern browsers automatically block to protect user experience.
Omitting the 'controls' attribute, rendering the media completely inaccessible to users.
Specifying incorrect MIME types in <source type='...'> elements.
revision_checklist: Is 'controls' specified on all student-facing <video> and <audio> elements?
Is 'muted' paired with 'autoplay' whenever automated playback is required?
Is a responsive poster image configured for the video preview?
Does the <iframe> embed include an accessible title attribute and allowfullscreen?
